questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Compassion fatigue and whether our compassion has limits
How doctors and nurses treat coronavirus patients in hospital
The history of the charity Médecins Sans Frontières in Africa
How to raise money for charity by running a marathon
questions.why: Rob says compassion fatigue is the topic of this programme.

questions.q: Which example of compassion during the pandemic does Sam give?
options: Reading more news online
Working longer hours in the office
Helping elderly relatives and neighbours
Travelling to help in other countries
questions.why: Sam mentions people helping elderly relatives and neighbours and wearing masks.

questions.q: Who has compassion fatigue long been a problem for?
options: Journalists who report on wars
People in medical jobs
Teachers
Politicians
questions.why: Rob says it has long been a problem for people working in medical professions.

questions.q: According to Margaret Heffernan, why can caring for others be unhealthy for the carer?
options: Carers usually don't get paid enough for their work
Carers often catch diseases from the people they help
Carers don't have enough time to eat or sleep properly
It means taking on other people's pain yourself
questions.why: Sam says caring means taking on someone's pain yourself, which can have unhealthy consequences.

questions.q: What happens to people who read a lot of depressing news online, according to Heffernan?
options: They start helping more people
They stop using the internet
They become numb but also addicted to it
They feel happier about their own lives
questions.why: She says they become more and more numb and also more and more addicted to it.

questions.q: Why does Heffernan describe this as 'learned helplessness'?
options: People see upsetting things they feel they can't change
People slowly learn how to help others by using the internet
People are taught at school to ignore bad news on television
People need help from others to use new technology
questions.why: She says 'I'm consuming something that's upsetting me but I cannot do anything about it.'

questions.q: How is Tom Rivett-Carnac's view different from the idea that compassion is limited?
options: He thinks compassion is not important
He thinks only doctors can feel compassion
He thinks the news helps us feel more compassion
He sees compassion as a habit that can be developed
questions.why: He says, 'I also think compassion is a habit.'

questions.q: On what point do Tom Rivett-Carnac and Margaret Heffernan agree?
options: Compassion is fixed and cannot grow
The news media is part of the problem
People should stop caring for others
Social media helps build good habits
questions.why: Sam says, like Heffernan, Tom believes the news media is part of the problem.
